teams.heading: Steve Borthwick secures rule alignment boost for England World Cup campaign
teams.body: Steve Borthwick has secured a boost to his preparations for next year's tournament after Prem Rugby agreed to overhaul refereeing interpretations for the coming season. The Guardian understands agreement has been reached to better align domestic officiating with the international game, specifically targeting the offside line, the scrum's brake-foot law, and the breakdown. Borthwick previously met with directors of rugby following concerns over the consistency of officiating, aiming to mount a serious challenge to South Africa's supremacy in Australia.

teams.heading: France and league governing body face scrutiny over leaked World Cup workload list

The revelations have sparked debate among supporters over potential impacts on club campaigns and notable omissions from the list.

teams.heading: Ireland Women head coach Scott Bemand rues frustrating defeat against USA
teams.body: Ireland Women head coach Scott Bemand admitted their 40-36 defeat against the USA in the WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium was "a game we should have won". Bemand's side surrendered a 19-point advantage after leading 31-12 in the second half, as a loss of discipline and four unanswered tries from the visitors turned the fixture. A late try from Dorothy Wall in the red gave Ireland a final chance to snatch victory, but the USA defence held firm.

teams.heading: Italy And South Africa To Clash At Turin's Allianz Stadium
teams.body: Top-level international rugby returns to the Allianz Stadium as Juventus' home ground prepares to host Italy against reigning world champions South Africa in November. Gonzalo Quesada's side begins their November series in Turin before facing Argentina in Genoa and Fiji in Udine, following three away matches during the summer against Japan, New Zealand and Australia. Giorgio Chiellini noted the stadium continues to demonstrate its vocation for hosting major events and its role as a point of reference for the local area.

teams.heading: Wales Women Lose Seren Lockwood To Injury Ahead Of USA Test
teams.body: Scrum-half Seren Lockwood has been ruled out of Wales Women's second fixture against the USA at Cardiff Arms Park after failing a head injury assessment during the victory over South Africa. Lockwood's absence forces a reshuffle in the backline, with Lleucu George returning at fly-half and Keira Bevan reverting to scrum-half. Head coach Sean Lynn acknowledged the setback, stating, "It's always sad to see an individual coming off, but the HIA is great to have on board, we're looking after her."

teams.heading: Argentina men secure gold medal victory at South American Games
teams.body: Argentina captured the gold medal at the 2026 Juegos Suramericanos rugby sevens tournament after recording a hard-fought 17-7 victory over Chile in the final at the Hipódromo in Rosario. Following a severe storm that forced tournament organisers to push the final fixtures back by a day, the hosts delivered a clinical display on home soil to cement their regional dominance. The victory also secures automatic qualification for the 2027 Pan American Games in Lima.

teams.heading: Harry Potter And The Wallabies Wait Out Springboks Selection
teams.body: Australia winger Harry Potter has taken a cheeky dig at South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus after the Springboks made 13 changes to their starting XV for Sunday's clash in Perth. Asked whether knowing the opposition lineup so early offered an advantage, Potter joked, "Well, we'll wait for the 23 to be absolutely confirmed." While Erasmus has a history of making late alterations on the eve of his team's matches, Potter is still expecting a formidable challenge from a visiting side featuring numerous World Cup winners.

teams.heading: Naoto Saito leads Japan past Fiji to claim Pacific Nations title
teams.body: The Brave Blossoms secured their first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019 with a hard-fought 20-15 victory over holders Fiji at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium. Captain and player of the tournament Naoto Saito called the win a great breakthrough to create history for Japan. Mamoru Harada and Ben Gunter scored tries, while Sam Greene added vital points as Japan withstood fierce physicality to claim their fifth win against Fiji and move into the world top ten.

teams.heading: New Zealand captain Ardie Savea faces lengthy spell following shoulder operation
teams.body: All Blacks skipper Ardie Savea is set for a lengthy stint on the sidelines after New Zealand Rugby announced he will undergo surgery on a dislocated shoulder. Savea sustained the injury during the first half of the third Test against the Springboks in Soweto. Furthermore, New Zealand's injury list has deepened with Luke Jacobson ruled out for four to five months following elbow surgery and winger Caleb Clarke sidelined for five months with a ruptured shoulder tendon.

teams.heading: Andre Esterhuizen captains changed Springboks side against the Wallabies
teams.body: Head coach Rassie Erasmus has made 13 changes to his starting XV for Sunday's clash in Perth, naming Andre Esterhuizen as captain in the absence of Siya Kolisi. The 32-year-old centre leads an overhauled lineup featuring only two survivors from the victory over the All Blacks in Baltimore, with Eben Etzebeth and Ethan Hooker retained in the run-on team. “He captained the Hollywoodbets Sharks, and he has brought so much to our squad off and on the field,” Erasmus said of his new skipper.
